preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip())
preconditions.description: Every non-empty line in stdin is a valid string (no whitespace-only lines).
The first line of stdin is a positive integer T (number of test cases).
Each test case consists of exactly two lines: an integer N (length of string) followed by the string S.
For each test case, the first line is a positive integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 2e5).

preconditions.expression: all(len(S) == int(N) for N, S in [(test_case.split()[0], test_case.split()[1]) for test_case in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string S has length exactly equal to the integer N.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c.islower() for c in S) for N, S in [(test_case.split()[0], test_case.split()[1]) for test_case in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: Each character in S is a lowercase English letter.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) == len(S) for output_line, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [test_case.split()[1] for test_case in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]))
postconditions.description: Each output line has the same length as the corresponding input string S.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c.islower() for c in output_line) for output_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output line consists only of lowercase English letters.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == sorted(S, key=lambda x: (ord(x),)) if all(abs(ord(S[i]) - ord(S[i+1])) == 1 for i in range(len(S)-1)) else any(output_line == ''.join(sorted(S, key=lambda x: (ord(x),))) for S in [S]) for output_line, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [test_case.split()[1] for test_case in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the lexicographically smallest string obtainable by swapping adjacent characters (where adjacent means |ord(S[i]) - ord(S[i+1])| == 1) any number of times. This is equivalent to sorting the string in ascending order if all adjacent characters in the original string are adjacent in the alphabet (i.e., |ord(S[i]) - ord(S[i+1])| == 1 for all i). Otherwise, the output is the sorted string (since any permutation can be achieved via adjacent swaps if the adjacency condition is not globally satisfied).

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == ''.join(sorted(S)) for output_line, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [test_case.split()[1] for test_case in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]))
postconditions.description: The output line for each test case is the lexicographically smallest permutation of the input string S, achievable by any sequence of adjacent swaps (where adjacent means |ord(S[i]) - ord(S[i+1])| == 1). This is always the sorted string because the adjacency condition allows any permutation (e.g., bubble sort-like swaps can rearrange the string fully).
